🚨🚨NEW PREPRINT ALERT!🚨🚨Proud to present our recent study, out now on bioRxiv, in which we reveal an RNA-dependent positive feedback loop that drives malignant ribosome biogenesis and tumour growth (1/15). 🔗 www.biorxiv.org/content/10.6...

7:18 PM · Jul 3, 2026

Everybody can reply

4 saves

2

27

48

Faraz Mardakheh's avatar

Nucleolus is the cell's factory for making ribosomes. Enlarged nucleoli have been recognized as a hallmark of cancer for over 100 years, but the molecular mechanism behind this phenomenon, and its functional relevance to tumourigenesis has remained elusive (2/15).

1

1

Faraz Mardakheh's avatar

We set out to study this using an inducible mouse model of pancreatic cancer driven by RAS oncogene. We found that RAS triggers coalescence of nucleoli into larger ones. This depends on activation of the downstream MAPK signalling (3/15).

1

Faraz Mardakheh's avatar

But does bigger mean any different? We used spatial proteomics and phosphoproteomics to reveal that that oncogenic RAS-MAPK signalling greatly alters the nucleolar proteome composition (4/15).

1

2

Faraz Mardakheh's avatar

Of the proteins that change in the nucleolus, one complex immediately stood out: Casein Kinase 2 (CK2) holoenzyme. CK2 is a constitutively active kinase with diverse cellular roles. We found that CK2 physically translocates to the nucleolus after oncogenic RAS-MAPK activation (5/15).
